question.text: The locus of the mid-points of the chords of the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}+2 x-2 y-2=0,$ which make an angle of $90^{\circ}$ at the centre is

solution.text: Given, equation of circle is $x^{2}+y^{2}+2 x-2 y-2=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad(x+1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}=4$ $\therefore$ Centre (-1,1) and radius $=2$ Let $(h, k)$ be the mid-point of chord. From figure, $$ O P=\sqrt{(h+1)^{2}+(k-1)^{2}} $$ $\ln \Delta O A P$ $$ \begin{aligned} \sin 45^{\circ}=& \frac{O P}{O A} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{(h+1)^{2}+(k-1)^{2}}}{2} \end{aligned} $$ On squaring both sides, we get $$ (h+1)^{2}+(k-1)^{2}=2 $$ $\Rightarrow \quad h^{2}+k^{2}+2 h-2 k=0$ $\therefore$ Locus of $P$ will be $$ x^{2}+y^{2}+2 x-2 y=0 $$
